newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS OUTCLASS FRANCE TO WIN FIRST TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS OUTCLASS FRANCE TO WIN FIRST TEST.

text.p: South Africa revived sweet memories by outclassing a depleted French side 22-12 in the first of two rugby union tests on a wet and windy afternoon on Saturday.
It was the first time the two teams clashed since the Springboks beat France 19-15 on another rainy day in their World Cup semifinal in June 1995 in Durban.
The visitors, playing impressive, powerful rugby, built their victory in the first half with two tries by James Small and Andre Joubert and three penalties by flyhalf Henry Honiball.
As the French had only managed two penalties by winger Richard Dourthe, the teams changed sides with the Springboks comfortably leading 19-6.

The home team tried their best to fight back into the match in the second half but failed to breach a tight South African defence and had to be content with two more penalties by Dourthe while Honiball scored one more for the world champions.
France, who had lost no fewer than six first-choice players in the build-up to the match in Bordeaux, made ook a fine start, opening the scoring in the second minute thanks to a Dourthe penalty.
But the Springboks reacted in the next minute with a powerful run along the line by winger Small for a try which Honiball failed to convert.

Dominating the lineouts and using mauls to gain ground, the South Africans stayed in the lead from then on and when their hosts tried to react, fine kicking by South African fullback Joubert sent them back into their half.

The home side, who had seen Olivier Merle, Olivier Roumat, Emile Ntamack, Philippe Saint-Andre, Thomas Cataignede and Alain Penaud all withdraw though injury in the last few days, were forced to field a young and largely untested team.
A fine move sparked by scrumhalf Joos van der Vesthuizen led to a dive in the corner by Joubert for the match's second try in the 32nd minute.

The French, who hardy saw the ball in the first half, recovered some pride in the last 40 minutes and came close to a try with a succession of scrums near the Springboks' line. But the South African defence resisted bravely.
A penalty by Dourthe in the 66th minute allowed France to reduce the arrears. They were behind 19-12 at that point and a converted try would have been enough to earn them victory.
But three minutes later, Honiball put over a penalty and the South Africans then held firm until the final whistle.

"We made very few mistakes and played well in difficult conditions, especially in the second half," said Springboks coach Andre Markgraaff. "You must give France credit for never giving up but I think we deserved to win.
His French counterpart Jean-Claude Skrela said his team had made far too many errors.
"When you make a lot of mistakes against a team like the Springboks, you can't expect to win," he said. "We were constantly under pressure, even if we did play better in the second half."
The South Africans go on to meet the French students in Lille on Tuesday before the second test next Saturday at Parc des Princes in Paris.

Teams France: 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny, 14-Richard Dourthe, 13-Stephane Glas (17-Christophe Lamaison), 12-Guillaume Bouic, 11-David Berty (16-David Vendittti 49th, 10-Laurent Mazas, 9-Philippe Carbonneau, 8-Thierry Labrousse (19-Richard Castel 57th), 7-Philippe Benetton, 6-Abdelatif Benazzi (cap), 5-Fabien Pelous, 4-Hugues Miorin, 3-Franck Tournaire, 2-Marc de Rougemont (21-Marc dal Maso 73rd), 1-Christian Califano. South Africa: 15-Andre Joubert, 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Hennie Le Roux, 11-Jacques Olivier, 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Vesthuizen, 8-Gary Teichmann (cap), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-James Dalton (21-Henry Tromp 76th), 1-Dawie Theron (20-Toks van der Linde 71st).
